setup: Set an adjustable bench to a 15 to 30-degree decline and secure your legs under the ankle pads.
Grasp a dumbbell in each hand using a neutral grip (palms facing each other) and lie back on the bench.
Press the dumbbells directly over your chest, maintaining a slight, fixed bend in your elbows.
steps: Lower the dumbbells outward to your sides in a wide, controlled arc, keeping the elbow angle fixed throughout.
Descend until you feel a gentle stretch across your lower chest and shoulders.
Engage your pectorals to reverse the motion along the same wide path until the weights return above your chest.
instructions.breathing: Inhale smoothly as you lower the dumbbells to open the chest; exhale as you bring the dumbbells back together at the top.
cues: Keep elbows slightly bent and locked
Squeeze the chest at the top

common_faults.fault: Turning the fly into a press by excessively bending and extending the elbows.
common_faults.correction: Lock a slight bend in your elbows from start to finish and move solely from the shoulder joint.

common_faults.fault: Overstretching the shoulders at the bottom.
common_faults.correction: Limit the depth of the descent so your elbows do not drop excessively below bench level.

precautions: Use moderate loads to prevent anterior shoulder strain.
Ensure your shins and ankles are firmly locked into the decline bench pads before lifting the weights.

name: Decline Dumbbell Fly

sources.title: wger: Fly With Dumbbells, Decline Bench

summary: An isolation exercise targeting the lower pectoralis major by performing wide arm arcs with dumbbells on a decline bench.
